decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation: “In the ‘Save a link’ box…paste any web address…and press Save.” Client: “Saving from a single web-address box feels right.”
decisions.note: Conforming URL-save decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation: “guessed a title from the address itself.” Client: “fetch the page’s real title automatically”; the requested card also includes a short description and site icon.
decisions.note: The initial address-derived metadata strategy diverged from automatic remote-page collection; the client supplied the expected behavior during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation enumerates title, address, and saved time and discusses possibly pulling the real title, but never presents collection of a preview image. The client requests title, description, tags, and icon but does not mention the missing preview image.
decisions.note: The preview-image component of automatic metadata collection was omitted and passed without being surfaced.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation offers either pulling the real title or letting the user type one. Client: “fetch the page’s real title automatically and let me change it.”
decisions.note: The reference requires both automatic collection and user editing; the client corrected the either/or presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation chooses “a title, the web address, and the time you saved it.” Client asks for “the real title, a short description, tags, and the site icon,” with address/time secondary.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing readability-first card fields during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation only describes saving and displaying the link. Client: “clicking the saved item should open the original page.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing revisit/navigation behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 revised presentation says cards fill with “a real title, a short description, [and] the site icon,” but still omits preview-image collection. Client replies, “Yes, this matches what I had in mind.”
decisions.note: A revised prototype still omitted the preview image; bare approval does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presentation provides a Rename button on an already-saved card but no way to edit collected title/description before saving. Client says renaming gives the desired control.
decisions.note: Post-save title editing conforms, but the required pre-save editing opportunity remains absent and unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presentation: clicking the title or site name opens “the original page in a new browser tab.” Client confirms it opens the original.
decisions.note: Conforming original-URL navigation decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation allows adding multiple tags and removing one with ×. Client approves the tagging interaction.
decisions.note: Conforming assignment and editing of bookmark tags.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 offers Version A free-form entry without existing-tag suggestions and Version B showing existing tags plus new-tag entry. Client selects Version B because “seeing existing tags will help me stay consistent.”
decisions.note: The offered alternatives differed on autocomplete/reuse; the client selected the reference-conforming alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 offers cards with visible tags versus Version C where tags are “behind a click.” Client selects visible-on-card tags because hiding them would impair scanning.
decisions.note: The client selected the alternative that exposes tags per list item.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 presentation initially treats notes as short inline reminders. Client requests “a longer write-up with simple Markdown formatting” and a full rendered note.
decisions.note: The client added the missing Markdown authoring and rendering requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 presentation supports raw Markdown entry and a fully rendered expandable note. Client: “This feels right.”
decisions.note: Conforming Markdown-note implementation in the revised prototype.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 6–7 present add/edit-note controls, with saved Markdown rendered afterward. Client confirms adding and editing are intuitive.
decisions.note: Conforming note-editing behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presentation explicitly searches “title, description, your notes, the site, and tags”; it does not state that the complete URL is searched. Client broadly approves “searching everything at once” without identifying the URL-field difference.
decisions.note: The presented field set omits full URL search; approval alone is not a capture.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presentation only has generic word/tag-content matching. Client requests “`#tag` for a specific tag.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing tag-query syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presentation describes word matching but no exact phrases. Client requests “quoted phrases for an exact match.”
decisions.note: The client added exact-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presentation only gives implicit all-word matching. Client requests “`AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, plus parentheses for combinations.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing Boolean query language and grouping.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presentation does not specify case handling. Client explicitly says, “Search should ignore capitalization.”
decisions.note: Case-insensitive matching was a missing search requirement supplied by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 presentation demonstrates `#reference` matching only bookmarks carrying that exact tag. Client approves the combined syntax.
decisions.note: Conforming tag-search syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 presentation demonstrates `"web apps"` as an exact phrase. Client says precise search feels dependable.
decisions.note: Conforming exact-phrase decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 presentation demonstrates AND/OR/NOT and parenthesized grouping. Client approves the combined approach.
decisions.note: The Boolean operations and grouping themselves conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 presentation: “Case doesn’t matter…`REFERENCE`…same results as lowercase.” Client says search feels dependable.
decisions.note: Conforming case-insensitive term matching.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 presentation requires operators in capitals so lowercase `and`/`or` remain literal. Client explicitly accepts the difference: “Requiring capitalized `AND`, `OR`, and `NOT` works for me and makes lowercase words behave predictably.”
decisions.note: The reference examples allow lowercase operators and require quoting an operator to search it literally. The client explicitly identified and accepted the capitals-only convention.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 presentation makes Read later an opt-in bookmark flag. Client: “The opt-in model fits.”
decisions.note: Conforming unread/read-later marking.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 presentation provides a Reading list tab containing only items marked To read. Client approves.
decisions.note: Conforming separate unread-bookmarks view.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 presentation says Mark as read removes the card from Reading list but keeps it in Library. Client repeats and approves that behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming read transition.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 presentation hides archived links from Library and Reading list while keeping them intact and restorable. Client confirms they should remain fully recoverable.
decisions.note: Conforming reversible archive behavior distinct from removal.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 presentation provides a separate Archive tab and limits archived-item searches to that tab. Client explicitly approves.
decisions.note: Conforming archive-only list and search scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 presentation automatically captures a persistent readable-content copy at save time, viewable independently of the live page. Client says automatic capture and readable preservation are right.
decisions.note: The regular-page snapshot behavior conforms at the functional level.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 describes a readable-content reader but does not establish whether the snapshot is stored locally as a single HTML file. The client discusses readable content versus pixel-perfect appearance, not storage packaging.
decisions.note: The record cannot establish conformity or divergence for the explicit local single-file HTML rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 initially says every link receives a readable-content copy. Client supplies the exception: “For a link that points directly to a PDF, I’d want the original PDF preserved.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the snapshot behavior for direct PDF URLs.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 revised presentation preserves regular pages as readable copies and direct PDFs as original files. Client: “exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Conforming PDF-versus-HTML snapshot rule after correction.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker says the original-goal capabilities are settled. Client objects that management is unfinished: “I still need to delete bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing delete operation at the management-flow gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 client responds to the claimed settled scope: “edit their address and description—not only the title.”
decisions.note: The client supplied missing URL and description editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 client responds to the claimed settled scope: “avoid creating a duplicate when I save an address that’s already in my library.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing duplicate-save convergence behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 14 presentation adds editable Title, Address, and Description fields; existing flows already edit tags and notes. Client says editing feels right.
decisions.note: Together with established tag/note controls, the bookmark fields are editable as required.

decisions.evidence: Round 14 presentation blocks a duplicate, displays “You’ve already saved this,” and provides Show it to jump to and highlight the existing editable card. Client approves the duplicate rules.
decisions.note: Highlighting the existing editable bookmark is a functionally equivalent guide toward editing rather than duplicating.

decisions.evidence: Round 14 presentation makes Delete permanent with confirmation and contrasts it with recoverable Archive. Client says permanent deletion with confirmation is enough.
decisions.note: Conforming delete behavior and archive/delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 presentation re-fetches page-derived details and a fresh saved copy after an address change while retaining tags and note. Client explicitly confirms that behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming revised address-edit behavior and associated metadata/snapshot handling.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 presents oversized-content handling as the large-library boundary but no collection sorting. Client says, “With hundreds of links, I’d need sorting—such as by date added or title.”
decisions.note: The client added missing sorting at the large-collection review.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 large-content presentation lacks collection-level selection/actions. Client requests multi-select tagging, read/unread, archive, and delete actions.
decisions.note: The client added the missing bulk-action facility.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 presentation has no whole-result action. Client requires applying an action to “every bookmark matching the current search, tag, or tab,” not the entire library.
decisions.note: The client added filtered-scope whole-collection bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 presentation supplies Newest, Oldest, and Title A–Z sorting. Client says these cover the ordering used most often.
decisions.note: Conforming list sorting.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 bulk toolbar offers Read later, Mark read, Add tag, Archive, and Delete but no remove-tag action. Client identifies the gap: “bulk tagging should let me remove a tag…as well as add one.”
decisions.note: The bulk-action set omitted tag removal; the client corrected it.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 presentation provides “Select all N in results for…” and names the active search/tab scope. Client says the named scope gives enough confidence.
decisions.note: Conforming whole-current-filter action scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 18 revised presentation adds Remove tag across selected links while leaving links without that tag unaffected. Client says this completes bulk tagging.
decisions.note: The revised bulk-action set conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 presentation says reading-list items, archives, and preserved copies do not expire automatically. Client confirms they remain until explicitly changed or deleted.
decisions.note: Conforming persistence semantics for unread state, archives, and snapshots.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 presentation defines the preserved copy as a fixed point-in-time snapshot. Client explicitly confirms newer capture must be user-initiated.
decisions.note: Conforming snapshot semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 specification gate claims “the full picture” and summarizes auto-enrichment with title and description, but the settled scope still contains no preview-image capture. Client only says the summary matches.
decisions.note: Preview-image metadata remained omitted at the specification gate; bare approval is not an explicit acceptance of the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 summary presents one-box immediate saving and later full editing, but no title/description editing before save. Client gives general approval.
decisions.note: The required pre-save edit opportunity remained absent at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 “full picture” includes visible tag chips and `#tag` query syntax but no action for selecting a tag to filter the list. Client broadly approves.
decisions.note: Specific-tag selection/filtering is distinct from typing `#tag` and remained absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 summary says search works “across everything,” but the settled explicit field list from Round 8 was title, description, note, site, and tags rather than the complete URL. Client does not surface the difference.
decisions.note: The earlier URL-field omission carried into the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 claims “the full picture” and enumerates preserved-copy behavior but includes no Internet Archive capture. Client only gives overall approval.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot support was omitted from the declared complete specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 claims all flows are settled but presents no saved bundle combining a search term with included/excluded tags. Client only says the summary matches.
decisions.note: Saved filter bundles were omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 complete-scope summary contains no Netscape HTML import flow. Client broadly approves the summary.
decisions.note: Bookmark import was omitted from the declared complete scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 complete-scope summary contains no Netscape HTML export flow. Client broadly approves the summary.
decisions.note: Bookmark export was omitted from the declared complete scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 complete-scope summary contains no user settings for default sort, displayed items, font size, or similar display preferences. Client broadly approves.
decisions.note: Personal display settings were omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 implementation review describes “auto-fetched title/description” and an exhaustive confirmed-feature list, but still does not include preview-image collection. Client accepts the cycle without identifying this difference.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation realizes the previously incomplete metadata decision; this is a distinct implementation-review opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 delivered-feature list says “full edit” after saving but presents no editing of auto-collected title/description before save. Client gives cycle-level approval only.
decisions.note: Pre-save editing remains absent in the delivered behavior as presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 delivered-feature list includes visible tags and `#tag` search but no selecting a tag chip/control to filter. Client does not mention the difference.
decisions.note: Specific-tag selection/filtering remains absent at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 claims the agreed search implementation is complete; the agreed explicit search fields inherited from Round 8 omit the full URL. Client provides bare completion approval.
decisions.note: Full-text URL coverage remains unexpressed in the implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 exhaustive “What it does” and verification lists include local preserved copies but no Internet Archive capture. Client accepts the software as complete for the cycle.
decisions.note: Internet Archive capture is absent from the delivered feature set; general acceptance does not qualify as accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 exhaustive delivered-feature and test lists contain no saved search/tag bundles. Client gives general completion approval.
decisions.note: Bundles remain absent at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 exhaustive delivered-feature and verification lists contain no Netscape HTML import. Client gives general completion approval.
decisions.note: Import remains absent at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 exhaustive delivered-feature and verification lists contain no Netscape HTML export. Client gives general completion approval.
decisions.note: Export remains absent at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 exhaustive delivered-feature and verification lists contain no display-related user settings. Client gives general completion approval.
decisions.note: Personal display settings remain absent at implementation review.
